story.title: FBI Investigates Breach of National Crime Information Center Database
story.summary: The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of its National Crime Information Center database, which is utilized by law enforcement agencies to share critical information. Reports indicate that hackers may have compromised the database, prompting the bureau to examine the entry point and assess what data may have been affected. This incident marks the second cyberattack on the FBI in recent months.

explore_lenses.label: Why would an NCIC breach matter nationally?
explore_lenses.title: A shared operational system is at issue
explore_lenses.summary: NCIC is not a single-agency archive: it is the FBI-operated system through which authorized agencies across the country exchange time-sensitive criminal-justice records. Its importance lies in both the sensitivity of the data and officers’ reliance on timely, accurate search results.

claims.text: The FBI's privacy assessment says NCIC links criminal and authorized noncriminal justice agencies in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, U.S. territories, select foreign countries, and operates around the clock.

Authorized users query NCIC for functions including fugitive apprehension, missing-person cases, stolen-property recovery, protection orders, sex-offender monitoring, and firearms- and weapons-related background checks.

NCIC's records are supplied by participating agencies, which are responsible for their accuracy, timeliness, and completeness; that shared structure means any confirmed integrity problem could require coordination beyond the FBI.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: As of November 21, 2026, reporting had not established whether the suspected intrusion disrupted access for agencies or affected the accuracy of any NCIC record.

explore_lenses.label: Was information exposed, changed, or both?
explore_lenses.title: The key distinction is confidentiality versus integrity
explore_lenses.summary: The reported investigation does not yet show whether an intruder viewed or removed records, changed them, or merely reached part of the system. Those outcomes would pose different risks for people in the database and for officers using it.

claims.text: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack, but the bureau declined public comment and the scope was not immediately clear, according to an AP source familiar with the matter.

FBI CJIS policy classifies criminal-justice information as including biometric, identity-history, biographic, property, and case or incident-history data; NCIC also contains restricted files subject to heightened access and dissemination rules.

A former FBI official told CNN that the central concern extends beyond possible data exposure to whether attackers could compromise the accuracy of information officers rely on; no altered records have been publicly reported.

explore_lenses.label: What will investigators need to establish next?
explore_lenses.title: Attribution and scope remain open questions
explore_lenses.summary: The next meaningful findings would distinguish a confirmed compromise from a suspected intrusion and determine its operational consequences. They will also show whether this incident has any connection to the FBI's separate September job-portal breach.

claims.text: AP reported that the apparent NCIC hack was first reported by CNN and independently confirmed by a person familiar with the matter; the FBI had not publicly described the incident by November 21, 2026.
The FBI's official NCIC assessment says the system is operated by the FBI's CJIS Division, while a CJIS Advisory Policy Board gives the FBI director recommendations on NCIC operational principles.

The September incident involved an FBI job portal and claims by the ShinyHunters group about employee and applicant data; available reporting does not establish a connection between that event and the reported NCIC intrusion.

story_report.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center, a law-enforcement database used by federal, state and local agencies. The bureau declined public comment, and the scope of the suspected intrusion was not immediately clear. The immediate consequence is an investigation into what, if any, information or systems were affected in a network that supports frontline criminal-justice operations; public reporting had not identified an attacker or established whether records were altered.

sections.heading: National Crime Information Center Operations
sections.body: NCIC links criminal-justice and authorized noncriminal-justice agencies across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, U.S. territories, select foreign countries and operates around the clock. Authorized users consult it for fugitive apprehensions, missing-person cases, stolen-property recovery, protection orders, sex-offender monitoring, and firearms- and weapons-related background checks. The FBI’s Criminal Justice Information Services Division operates the system, with an advisory board providing recommendations on operational principles.

sections.heading: Potential Risks to Crime Data
sections.body: FBI policy defines criminal-justice information broadly to include biometric, identity-history, biographic, property, and case or incident-history data, while NCIC also contains restricted files governed by heightened access and dissemination rules. Participating agencies supply NCIC records and are responsible for their accuracy, timeliness and completeness. A former FBI official told CNN the concern is not only possible data exposure but also whether information officers rely on could be compromised; no altered records have been publicly reported.

unresolved.text: Public reporting had not identified an attacker, the means of entry, affected NCIC files, the number of records accessed, or whether any records were modified.
It was not established whether the suspected intrusion disrupted agency access to NCIC or affected the accuracy of any record.
It remained unclear whether the FBI would issue a public assessment, notify affected agencies or individuals, attribute responsibility, or announce corrective actions.

related_stories.summary: Harry Kane, the England captain and Bayern Munich striker, has shared an image from his hospital bed following surgery for a torn ligament in his left ankle. He sustained the injury during a match on Friday and has expressed his determination to return for the 'business end of the season.'

related_stories.title: Capture of 'El Chapo Isidro' Triggers Violence in Sinaloa
related_stories.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, was arrested by Mexican special forces in Sinaloa. His capture has led to a surge of violence in the region, including gunfire and burning vehicles, causing panic among civilians. The operation reportedly involved cooperation with US intelligence.
